Due to feedback and processing delays, the obtained CSI may be outdated before its actual usage, namely ![images](images/c16-i0230.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>&#8800;</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>&#964;</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, which probably will degrade the performance of adaptive transmission systems severely. The task of MIMO channel prediction is to get a predicted value ![images](images/c16-i0231.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>&#964;</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> that approximates ![images](images/c16-i0232.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>&#964;</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> as closely as possible.

 

#### 16.5.3.1 Channel Gain Prediction

Analogous to a single‐antenna system, a complex‐valued RNN needs to be employed to deal with complex channel gains of a MIMO system. At time ![images](images/c16-i0233.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0234.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> is obtained through channel estimation. To adapt to the input layer of a RNN, the channel matrix is required to be vectorized into a ![images](images/c16-i0235.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#215;</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> vector, as follows:

(16.36)![equation](images/c16-math-0037.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mover accent="true"> <mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi> <mo>&#8594;</mo> </mover> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <msub> <mi>h</mi> <mn>11</mn> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>h</mi> <mn>12</mn> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>,</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>h</mi> <mrow> <msub> <mi>N</mi> <mi>r</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>N</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

Together with a number of ![images](images/c16-i0236.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> past values ![images](images/c16-i0237.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, the external input of RNN this case is ![images](images/c16-i0238.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, resulting in a multi‐step predictive value ![images](images/c16-i0239.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, which can be transformed to a predicted channel matrix ![images](images/c16-i0240.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>.

Similar to a SISO channel, a real‐valued RNN can be applied to predict the real and imaginary parts of a channel matrix separately so as to lower complexity and improve accuracy. Accordingly, a channel matrix ![images](images/c16-i0241.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi></mrow></math> (time index dropped for brevity) can be decomposed into

(16.37)![equation](images/c16-math-0038.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi> <mi>R</mi> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <mi>j</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi> <mi>I</mi> </msub> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c16-i0242.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>&#8476;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mi>r</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>&#215;</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></math> denotes a matrix composed of the real parts of channel gains and ![images](images/c16-i0243.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mi>I</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>&#8465;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>&#215;</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is its imaginary counterpart. Also, these matrices are required to be vectorized, e.g.

(16.38)![equation](images/c16-math-0039.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi> <mi>r</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi> <mo>&#8594;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>R</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""> <mrow> <msubsup> <mi>h</mi> <mn>11</mn> <mi>r</mi> </msubsup> <mo>,</mo> <msubsup> <mi>h</mi> <mn>12</mn> <mi>r</mi> </msubsup> <mo>,</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>,</mo> <msubsup> <mi>h</mi> <mrow> <msub> <mi>N</mi> <mi>r</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>N</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> </mrow> <mi>r</mi> </msubsup> </mrow> </mfenced> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

Without the necessity of using two RNNs, the real and imaginary parts can be processed jointly in a single predictor, enabled by an external input as ![images](images/c16-i0244.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></mfenced></mrow></math>. Together with the feedback, the predictive output ![images](images/c16-i0245.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></mfenced></mrow></math> is available and transformed into the predicted real and imaginary matrices ![images](images/c16-i0246.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>R</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c16-i0247.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>I</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, respectively. Then, a multi‐step predicted channel matrix for time ![images](images/c16-i0248.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> is reached simply by applying ![images](images/c16-i0249.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>R</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>j</mi><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>I</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>.

 

#### 16.5.3.2 Channel Envelope Prediction

As mentioned previously, only the envelope of a channel gain, rather than the gain itself, is required by some adaptive transmission systems, where the prediction of channel gains can be avoided so as to lower complexity, speed up the training process, and improve accuracy. Let ![images](images/c16-i0250.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>&#215;</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></math> denote a matrix in which the ![images](images/c16-i0251.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> entry is the envelope of the channel between transmit antenna ![images](images/c16-i0252.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> and receive antenna ![images](images/c16-i0253.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math>, denoted by ![images](images/c16-i0254.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo></mrow></math>. In order to adapt the input layer of a RNN, this matrix needs to be vectorized:

(16.39)![equation](images/c16-math-0040.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold">q</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mover accent="true"> <mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi> <mo>&#8594;</mo> </mover> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <msub> <mi>h</mi> <mn>11</mn> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <mo>,</mo> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <msub> <mi>h</mi> <mn>12</mn> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <mo>,</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>,</mo> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <msub> <mi>h</mi> <mrow> <msub> <mi>N</mi> <mi>r</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>N</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> </mrow> </mfenced> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

The matrix ![images](images/c16-i0255.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> at time ![images](images/c16-i0256.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>, as well as its delays ![images](images/c16-i0257.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, are fed into the RNN predictor as the external input, which thus is rewritten as ![images](images/c16-i0258.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">q</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">q</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">q</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>. The RNN output is then a predicted channel vector at ![images](images/c16-i0259.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math> steps ahead, i.e. ![images](images/c16-i0260.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">q</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, which can be transformed into ![images](images/c16-i0261.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">Q</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>.

 

### 16.5.4 Frequency‐Selective MIMO Prediction

The discrete‐time baseband equivalent model for a single‐antenna system in a frequency‐ selective channel is given by

(16.40)![equation](images/c16-math-0041.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>r</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>=</mo> <munderover> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>l</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>L</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </munderover> <msub> <mi>h</mi> <mi>l</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mi>s</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>l</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>+</mo> <mi>n</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c16-i0262.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> denotes the ![images](images/c16-i0263.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>l</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> tap for a time‐varying channel filter, ![images](images/c16-i0264.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c16-i0265.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> represent the transmitted and received signals at time ![images](images/c16-i0266.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>, respectively, and ![images](images/c16-i0267.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> is additive noise. Dropping the time index for simplicity, a frequency‐selective channel is modeled as a linear channel filter ![images](images/c16-i0268.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow></math>, where ![images](images/c16-i0269.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow></math> is the filter length. This channel can be converted into ![images](images/c16-i0270.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> orthogonal flat‐fading sub‐carriers by means of the OFDM modulation (Jiang and Kaiser, [2016](#c16.xhtml#c16-bib-0014)). The signal transmission over the ![images](images/c16-i0271.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> sub‐carrier at time ![images](images/c16-i0272.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> can be modeled as

[(16.41)](#c16.xhtml#c16-R_disp-0042)![equation](images/c16-math-0042.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>r</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>s</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>&#241;</mi> <mi>n</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>,</mo> <mspace width="2.22198pt"/> <mspace width="2.22198pt"/> <mi>n</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mi>&#8230;</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>N</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c16-i0273.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0274.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, and ![images](images/c16-i0275.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#241;</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> stand for the transmitted signal, received signal, and noise, respectively, in the frequency domain. According to the picket fence effect in discrete Fourier transform (DFT) (Oppenheim and Schafer, [1975](#c16.xhtml#c16-bib-0029)), the frequency response of the channel filter denoted by ![images](images/c16-i0276.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow></math> is the DFT of ![images](images/c16-i0277.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow></math>, which is the filter ![images](images/c16-i0278.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi></mrow></math> padding with ![images](images/c16-i0279.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></math> zeros at the tail.

The extension of Eq. ([16.41](#c16.xhtml#c16-disp-0042)) to a multi‐antenna system with ![images](images/c16-i0280.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> transmit and ![images](images/c16-i0281.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math> receive antennas is straightforward by applying the same OFDM modulation into MIMO channels. Thus, on the ![images](images/c16-i0282.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> sub‐carrier, the signal transmission is represented by

(16.42)![equation](images/c16-math-0043.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi mathvariant="bold">s</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi mathvariant="bold">n</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>,</mo> <mspace width="2.22198pt"/> <mspace width="2.22198pt"/> <mi>n</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mi>&#8230;</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>N</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c16-i0283.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> represents ![images](images/c16-i0284.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math> received symbols for sub‐carrier ![images](images/c16-i0285.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> at time ![images](images/c16-i0286.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0287.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">s</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> corresponding to ![images](images/c16-i0288.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> transmit symbols, and ![images](images/c16-i0289.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">n</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> is a vector of additive noise. The matrix ![images](images/c16-i0290.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msubsup><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>&#215;</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></math> consists of the frequency responses of all subchannels on sub‐carrier ![images](images/c16-i0291.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> at time ![images](images/c16-i0292.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> denoted by ![images](images/c16-i0293.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="double-struck">C</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, where ![images](images/c16-i0294.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>&#8804;</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c16-i0295.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&#8804;</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>. The frequency response for the subchannel between transmit antenna ![images](images/c16-i0296.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> and receive antenna ![images](images/c16-i0297.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math>, i.e. ![images](images/c16-i0298.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msubsup><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mn>0</mn><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mn>1</mn><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow></math>, can be derived by conducting DFT on its channel filter denoted by ![images](images/c16-i0299.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mn>0</mn><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow></math>.

[Figure 16.8](#c16.xhtml#c16-fig-0008) illustrates the block diagram of a frequency‐domain predictor proposed in (Jiang and Schotten, [2019b](#c16.xhtml#c16-bib-0018)). The main idea is to convert a frequency‐selective channel into a set of orthogonal flat‐fading sub‐carriers and then utilize a frequency‐domain predictor to forecast the frequency response on each sub‐carrier. Using a series of channel samples over an arbitrary sub‐carrier ![images](images/c16-i0300.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mfenced open="|" close="" separators=""><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo></mrow></math> to train a network, the trained RNN can be applied to predict unknown samples. At time ![images](images/c16-i0301.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> over sub‐carrier ![images](images/c16-i0302.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>, as shown in [Figure 16.8](#c16.xhtml#c16-fig-0008), the current CSI ![images](images/c16-i0303.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, as well as its ![images](images/c16-i0304.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></math>‐step delays ![images](images/c16-i0305.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, are fed into the RNN. To adapt the input layer, these matrices need to be vectorized as:

![Figure 16.8 Illustration of a frequency‐domain predictor for frequency‐selective multi‐antenna channels.](images/c16f008.jpg)

[Figure 16.8](#c16.xhtml#R_c16-fig-0008) Illustration of a frequency‐domain predictor for frequency‐selective multi‐antenna channels.

(16.43)![equation](images/c16-math-0044.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mtext>vec</mtext> <mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""> <mrow> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> </msub> </mrow> </mfenced> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <msubsup> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> <mn>11</mn> </msubsup> <mo>,</mo> <msubsup> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> <mn>12</mn> </msubsup> <mo>,</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>,</mo> <msubsup> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> <mrow> <msub> <mi>N</mi> <mi>r</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>N</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> </mrow> </msubsup> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> </mrow> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

which is implemented through a matrix‐to‐vector module as shown in the figure. Together with the feedback from the output denoted by ![images](images/c16-i0306.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msubsup><mi>&#293;</mi><mi>n</mi><mn>11</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>&#293;</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow></math>, the whole input is thus ![images](images/c16-i0307.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c16-i0308.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>. The RNN outputs a ![images](images/c16-i0309.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>D</mi></mrow></math>‐step prediction, i.e. ![images](images/c16-i0310.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msubsup><mi>&#293;</mi><mi>n</mi><mn>11</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>&#293;</mi><mi>n</mi><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow></math>, which can be recovered to a predicted matrix ![images](images/c16-i0311.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> by a vector‐to‐matrix module.

From the perspective of a pilot‐assisted system, only a subset of sub‐carriers instead of all ![images](images/c16-i0312.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> sub‐carriers needs to be predicted if the frequency correlation of channels is utilized. Suppose one pilot is inserted uniformly every ![images](images/c16-i0313.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow></math> sub‐carriers, which amounts to a total of ![images](images/c16-i0314.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="&#8968;" close="&#8969;" separators=""><mrow><mfrac><mi>N</mi><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></mrow></math> pilot sub‐carriers, where ![images](images/c16-i0315.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo>&#8968;</mo><mo>&#183;</mo><mo>&#8969;</mo></mrow></math> denotes a ceiling function. Given their predicted CSI ![images](images/c16-i0316.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0317.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></math>, and supposing the indices of pilot sub‐carriers are ![images](images/c16-i0318.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow></math>, for example, the prediction for all sub‐carriers ![images](images/c16-i0319.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0320.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> can be obtained by interpolating ![images](images/c16-i0321.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>.

 

### 16.5.5 Prediction‐Assisted MIMO‐OFDM

To further shed light on the mechanism of channel prediction, transmit antenna selection in a MIMO system with ![images](images/c16-i0322.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> transmit and ![images](images/c16-i0323.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></math> receive antennas in a frequency‐selective fading channel is depicted as a representative application example. A frequency‐selective channel can be converted into ![images](images/c16-i0324.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> orthogonal flat‐fading sub‐carriers by means of a fast Fourier transform (FFT) demodulator at the receiver and an inverse FFT (IFFT) modulator at the transmitter, in combination with the utilization of cyclic prefix (CP), as shown in [Figure 16.9](#c16.xhtml#c16-fig-0009). There exist two selection strategies for TAS: bulk or per‐tone, as mentioned in (Zhang and Nabar, [2008](#c16.xhtml#c16-bib-0045)). Without loss of generality, the latter is used for a clear illustration, i.e. each sub‐carrier decides its best antenna individually instead of the same selection for all sub‐carriers.

An OFDM symbol carries a payload of ![images](images/c16-i0325.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> data symbols denoted by ![images](images/c16-i0326.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">d</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow></math>, while the remaining ![images](images/c16-i0327.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> sub‐carriers are reserved for comb‐type pilot symbols that are uniformly inserted in sub‐carriers ![images](images/c16-i0328.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow></math>, where ![images](images/c16-i0329.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c16-i0330.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>P</mi></msub></mrow></math> is the interval of pilots. Through estimating the ![images](images/c16-i0331.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> pilot, the frequency response on pilot sub‐carrier ![images](images/c16-i0332.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> denoted by ![images](images/c16-i0333.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> can be known at the receiver. Taking advantage of the channel's frequency correlation, frequency‐domain interpolation is conducted to recover the CSI on all sub‐carriers, i.e. ![images](images/c16-i0334.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0335.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. Following the per‐tone selection scheme (Zhang and Nabar, [2008](#c16.xhtml#c16-bib-0045)), each data sub‐carrier chooses its own transmit antenna(s). Analogous to Eq. ([16.1](#c16.xhtml#c16-disp-0001)), the traditional TAS system directly applies outdated CSI ![images](images/c16-i0336.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> to select a single antenna with the largest channel gain in sub‐carrier ![images](images/c16-i0337.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>, following

(16.44)![equation](images/c16-math-0045.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>&#951;</mi> <mi>n</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="normal">arg</mi> <mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi> </mrow> <mrow> <mn>1</mn> <mo>&#8804;</mo> <msub> <mi>n</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>&#8804;</mo> <msub> <mi>N</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> </mrow> </msub> <msup> <mrow> <mfenced open="&#8214;" close="&#8214;" separators=""> <mrow> <msubsup> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> <mrow> <msub> <mi>n</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> </mrow> </msubsup> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> </mrow> </mfenced> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> </msup> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c16-i0338.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#951;</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> represents the index of the best antenna at time ![images](images/c16-i0339.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> for sub‐carrier ![images](images/c16-i0340.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0341.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">h</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> is the ![images](images/c16-i0342.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi>n</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> column vector of ![images](images/c16-i0343.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, and ![images](images/c16-i0344.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo>&#8741;</mo><mo>&#183;</mo><mo>&#8741;</mo></mrow></math> stands for the Euclidean norm of a vector. The receiver feeds the set of selected indices for all data sub‐carriers ![images](images/c16-i0345.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mfenced open="{" close="}" separators=""><mrow><msub><mi>&#951;</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>&#8739;</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8800;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow></math> back to the transmitter through a feedback channel. In the ![images](images/c16-i0346.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> sub‐carrier of OFDM symbol ![images](images/c16-i0347.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></math>, the TAS precoder allocates a data symbol to the best antenna ![images](images/c16-i0348.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#951;</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, while other antennas keep silent at this sub‐carrier.

Due to the channel fading, outdated CSI ![images](images/c16-i0349.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> may differ substantially from the actual value ![images](images/c16-i0350.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, leading to remarkable performance degradation (Yu et al., [2017](#c16.xhtml#c16-bib-0044)). With the aid of channel prediction, a selection decision can be made in terms of the predicted CSI that is possible to closely approximate the actual value. At time ![images](images/c16-i0351.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>, as depicted in [Figure 16.9](#c16.xhtml#c16-fig-0009), estimating the pilots at the ![images](images/c16-i0352.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> OFDM symbol can get the CSI of pilot sub‐carriers ![images](images/c16-i0353.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, fed into the channel predictor to extrapolate the predicted CSI ![images](images/c16-i0354.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>. A frequency‐domain interpolator is applied to obtain the CSI on all sub‐carriers denoted by ![images](images/c16-i0355.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0356.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> so as to replace ![images](images/c16-i0357.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="bold">H</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> to make decisions in a TAS system. Thus, the best antenna over sub‐carrier ![images](images/c16-i0358.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> can be selected as
