Here we assume that ![images](images/c19-i0046.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is i.i.d. with ![images](images/c19-i0047.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow></math>, and there exists a positive constant ![images](images/c19-i0048.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi></msub></mrow></math> such that ![images](images/c19-i0049.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8804;</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi></msub></mrow></math>.

Let ![images](images/c19-i0050.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">I</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> denote the ![images](images/c19-i0051.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi mathvariant="script"> U</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mo>&#215;</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi mathvariant="script"> F</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo></mrow></math> requested file type matrix in time slot ![images](images/c19-i0052.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c19-i0053.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">I</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8796;</mo><msub><mrow><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. Here ![images](images/c19-i0054.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> if the requested file type by UT ![images](images/c19-i0055.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math> is ![images](images/c19-i0056.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow></math> in time slot ![images](images/c19-i0057.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>, and 0 otherwise. We assume that each UT can request at most only one type of file in one time slot, which means that the row weight of ![images](images/c19-i0058.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">I</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is at most 1. The requested probability of each file ![images](images/c19-i0059.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="script">F</mi></mrow></math> is subject to Zipf distribution Zink et al. ([2009](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0058)).

 

##### *The Transmission Model*

The wireless channels between UTs and FANs are assumed to be flat‐fading channels Tse and Viswanath ([2005](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0041)), and all FANs transmit at constant power. We assume that the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) at the UTs follows Gaussian distribution with ![images](images/c19-i0060.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> N</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Note that the maximum service rate of UT ![images](images/c19-i0061.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math> can be obtained if it has been allocated the total bandwidth by its associated FAN. Then the maximum backlog that can be served in time slot ![images](images/c19-i0062.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> over link ![images](images/c19-i0063.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="script">E</mi></mrow></math> is given by

(19.2)![equation](images/c19-math-0002.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>C</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">T</mi> <msub> <mi>B</mi> <mi>h</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#183;</mo> <mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mi> <mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""> <mrow> <msub> <mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> <mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""> <mrow> <mn>1</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mfrac> <mrow> <msub> <mi>P</mi> <mi>h</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>g</mi> <mrow> <mi>h</mi> <mi>u</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <msub> <mi>s</mi> <mrow> <mi>h</mi> <mi>u</mi> </mrow> </msub> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <mn>2</mn> </msup> </mrow> <mrow> <msup> <mi>&#963;</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msup> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mo movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <msup> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">H</mi> <mo>\\</mo> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi>P</mi> <mrow> <msup> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi>g</mi> <mrow> <msup> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mi>u</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <msub> <mi>s</mi> <mrow> <msup> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mi>u</mi> </mrow> </msub> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <mn>2</mn> </msup> </mrow> </mfrac> </mrow> </mfenced> </mrow> </mfenced> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c19-i0064.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is the total bandwidth of FAN ![images](images/c19-i0065.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> in time slot ![images](images/c19-i0066.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>; ![images](images/c19-i0067.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow></math> is the transmit power of FAN ![images](images/c19-i0068.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></math>; ![images](images/c19-i0069.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is the large‐scale fading from FAN ![images](images/c19-i0070.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> to UT ![images](images/c19-i0071.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math>, which contains pathloss and shadow; and ![images](images/c19-i0072.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is the small‐scale fading, which follows the Rayleigh distribution. For simplicity, currently implemented rate adaption schemes Biglieri et al. ([1998](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0003)) Ong et al. ([2011](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0035)) are consistent in assuming slowly varying pathloss coefficients ![images](images/c19-i0073.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> change across slots in an i.i.d. manner, and each FAN ![images](images/c19-i0074.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> being aware of ![images](images/c19-i0075.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> for all ![images](images/c19-i0076.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="script">U</mi></mrow></math> at the beginning of each time slot ![images](images/c19-i0077.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>.

We also assume that each FAN ![images](images/c19-i0078.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> serves its associated UTs by using orthogonal FDMA or TDMA, which is consistent with most current wireless standards. Let ![images](images/c19-i0079.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#957;</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be the proportion of bandwidth allocated to UT ![images](images/c19-i0080.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math> by FAN ![images](images/c19-i0081.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></math>. Then ![images](images/c19-i0082.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#957;</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> satisfies ![images](images/c19-i0083.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&#60;</mo><msub><mi>&#957;</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8804;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> when ![images](images/c19-i0084.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, otherwise ![images](images/c19-i0085.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#957;</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. Denote ![images](images/c19-i0086.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#957;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8796;</mo><msub><mrow><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><mrow><msub><mi>&#957;</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> as the bandwidth allocation matrix, which is chosen from the feasible set ![images](images/c19-i0087.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> B</mi></mrow></math>,

(19.3)![equation](images/c19-math-0003.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="script"> B</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced open="{" close="}" separators=""> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#957;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <msubsup> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi> </mrow> <mrow> <mo>+</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> U</mi> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <mo>&#215;</mo> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> H</mi> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> </mrow> </msubsup> <mfenced open="|" close="" separators=""> <mrow> <mtable columnalign="left"> <mtr> <mtd class="array"> <msub> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">U</mi> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi>&#957;</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8804;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>;</mo> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd class="array"> <msub> <mi>&#957;</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mspace width="1em"/> <mtext>if</mtext> <mspace width="1em"/> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mspace width="1em"/> <mo>&#8704;</mo> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">H</mi> <mo>.</mo> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mrow> </mfenced> </mrow> </mfenced> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

Let ![images](images/c19-i0088.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> denote the amount of backlog that can be served for UT ![images](images/c19-i0089.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math> in time slot ![images](images/c19-i0090.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> with maximum value ![images](images/c19-i0091.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi></msub></mrow></math>, which is called the *service rate* hereafter. Define ![images](images/c19-i0092.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8796;</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi mathvariant="script"> U</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>. Note that each UT can associate with at most one FAN in a time slot, thus ![images](images/c19-i0093.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> can be expressed as follows:

[(19.4)](#c19.xhtml#c19-R_disp-0004)![equation](images/c19-math-0004.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>&#956;</mi> <mi>u</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <munder> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">H</mi> </mrow> </munder> <msub> <mi>C</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub> <mi>&#957;</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>,</mo> <mo>&#8704;</mo> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">U</mi> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math>  

##### *Queuing*

In each time slot, the arrived requests of all UTs will be queued in the request buffers at the FCN. We assume that FCN has ![images](images/c19-i0094.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi mathvariant="script"> F</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo></mrow></math> request buffers for each UT ![images](images/c19-i0095.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="script">U</mi></mrow></math>. Denote the queue length of the amount of request for file with type ![images](images/c19-i0096.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow></math> at the beginning of the ![images](images/c19-i0097.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>th time slot as ![images](images/c19-i0098.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Define ![images](images/c19-i0099.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>u</mi><mtext>sum</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8796;</mo><msub><mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="script"> F</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and denote ![images](images/c19-i0100.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi><mi>T</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>u</mi><mtext>sum</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8943;</mi><mspace width="0.3em"/><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi mathvariant="script"> U</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo></mrow><mtext>sum</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> as the queue length vector. We assume that all queues are initially empty, i.e. ![images](images/c19-i0101.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>&#8704;</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="script">U</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="script">F</mi></mrow></math>.

Let ![images](images/c19-i0102.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> denote the service rate for the requested file ![images](images/c19-i0103.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow></math> scheduled by the FCN according to a certain queuing discipline Huang et al. ([2016a](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0018)), such as FIFO, LIFO, or random discipline. We adopt the fully efficient scheduling policy given in Huang et al. ([2016a](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0018)) for queues, which means:

(19.5)![equation](images/c19-math-0005.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <munder> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>f</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> F</mi> </mrow> </munder> <msub> <mi>&#956;</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>f</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>&#956;</mi> <mi>u</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c19-i0104.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is defined in Eq. ([19.4](#c19.xhtml#c19-disp-0004)) and ![images](images/c19-i0105.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> if ![images](images/c19-i0106.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.

The queue length ![images](images/c19-i0107.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is updated in every time slot ![images](images/c19-i0108.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> according to the following rules:

(19.6)![equation](images/c19-math-0006.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>Q</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>f</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mrow> <mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""> <mrow> <msub> <mi>Q</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>f</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#956;</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>f</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </mfenced> </mrow> <mo>+</mo> </msup> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>A</mi> <mi>u</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#183;</mo> <msub> <mi>I</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>f</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c19-i0109.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo></mrow></math>.

The queuing process ![images](images/c19-i0110.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is stable if the following condition holds Neely ([2010](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0034)):

(19.7)![equation](images/c19-math-0007.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msubsup> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>Q</mi> <mo>&#175;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mtext>sum</mtext> </msubsup> <mo>=</mo> <munder> <mi mathvariant="normal">lim</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8594;</mo> <mi>&#8734;</mi> </mrow> </munder> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mi>t</mi> </mfrac> <munderover> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>&#964;</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </munderover> <mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <msubsup> <mi>Q</mi> <mi>u</mi> <mtext>sum</mtext> </msubsup> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>&#964;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>&#60;</mo> <mi>&#8734;</mi> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math>  

## 19.3 Problem Formulation and Analytical Framework

 

### Performance Metrics

We focus on the total throughput of the network. Therefore, we adopt the time‐averaged sum service rate of different UTs in the network as the performance metric, which is defined as follows:

(19.8)![equation](images/c19-math-0008.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>&#966;</mi> <mrow> <mi>a</mi> <mi>v</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8796;</mo> <mover accent="true"> <mrow> <mi>&#966;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#175;</mo> </mover> <mo>=</mo> <munder> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">U</mi> </mrow> </munder> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>&#956;</mi> <mo>&#175;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>u</mi> </msub> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c19-i0111.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>&#956;</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is the averaged expected service rate of UT ![images](images/c19-i0112.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math>.

To support for transmission latency sensitive applications, i.e. online video, service delay is a key metric that needs to be considered Ahlehagh and Dey ([2012](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0001)). According to Little's law Ross ([2014](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0037)), the average service delay experienced by each UT is proportional to the averaged amount of its unserved requests waiting at the FCN, which is the sum of the queue length for different files. Thus, the average delay per UT can be computed as the ratio between the average queue length and the mean traffic arrival rate, which is shown as follows:

(19.9)![equation](images/c19-math-0009.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#923;</mi> <mrow> <mi>a</mi> <mi>v</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8796;</mo> <mfrac> <mrow> <msub> <mo movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> U</mi> </mrow> </msub> <msubsup> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>Q</mi> <mo>&#175;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mtext>sum</mtext> </msubsup> </mrow> <mrow> <msub> <mo movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> U</mi> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mi>u</mi> </msub> </mrow> </mfrac> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math>  

### Average Network Throughput Maximization Problem

The system objective is to find a feasible FAN assignment ![images](images/c19-i0113.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and bandwidth allocation ![images](images/c19-i0114.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#957;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> to maximize the average network throughput while maintaining the stability of all the queues in the network. The average network throughput maximization problem can be formulated in ![images](images/c19-i0115.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">P</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>:

(19.10)![equation](images/c19-math-0010.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mtable columnalign="right left left"> <mtr> <mtd class="eqnarray-1"> <mi mathvariant="script">P</mi> <mn>1</mn> <mo>:</mo> <mspace width="1em"/> <munder> <mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>,</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#957;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </munder> </mtd> <mtd class="eqnarray-2"/> <mtd class="eqnarray-3"> <mover accent="true"> <mrow> <mi>&#966;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#175;</mo> </mover> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd class="eqnarray-1"> <mtext>s.t.</mtext> </mtd> <mtd class="eqnarray-2"/> <mtd class="eqnarray-3"> <msubsup> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>Q</mi> <mo>&#175;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mtext>sum</mtext> </msubsup> <mo>&#60;</mo> <mi>&#8734;</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mspace width="1em"/> <mo>&#8704;</mo> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">U</mi> <mo>,</mo> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd/> <mtd class="eqnarray-2"/> <mtd class="eqnarray-3"> <mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">A</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mspace width="1em"/> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#957;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> B</mi> <mspace width="1em"/> <mo>&#8704;</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo>,</mo> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mrow> </math> 

where the requirement of finite ![images](images/c19-i0116.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>u</mi><mtext>sum</mtext></msubsup></mrow></math> corresponds to the strong stability condition for all the queues Neely ([2010](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0034)). Queuing stability implies that buffered file requests are processed with finite delay. We will show that our proposed algorithms guarantee upper bounds for ![images](images/c19-i0117.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>&#175;</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and thus achieve the bounded service delay.

It is not difficult to identify that ![images](images/c19-i0118.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> P</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> is a highly challenging stochastic optimization problem with a large amount of stochastic information to be handled (including channel conditions and request buffer state information) and two optimization variables to be determined, which requires the design of an online operation and scheduling scheme for such a network. In addition, to maximize network throughput, it is essential to jointly optimize the FAN‐UT association and the resource allocation, which is always a complicated mixed integer programming problem. Further, the optimal decisions are temporally correlated due to the random‐arrival traffic demands. Furthermore, the FCN needs to reduce the delay per UT while maintaining the average network throughput, which requires the FCN to maintain a good balance between network throughput and average delay.

 

### Lyapunov Optimization‐Based Analytical Framework

In the following, we focus on solving this challenging problem ![images](images/c19-i0119.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">P</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> by using the Lyapunov optimization technique Neely ([2010](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0034)), with which we can transfer the challenging stochastic optimization problem ![images](images/c19-i0120.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> P</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> to be a deterministic per‐slot problem in each time slot.

We first define a quadratic Lyapunov function as follows:

(19.11)![equation](images/c19-math-0011.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>L</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8796;</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mn>2</mn> </mfrac> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mn>2</mn> </mfrac> <munder> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">U</mi> </mrow> </munder> <msup> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msubsup> <mi>Q</mi> <mi>u</mi> <mtext>sum</mtext> </msubsup> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> </msup> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

We then define a one‐slot conditional Lyapunov drift ![images](images/c19-i0121.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> as follows:

(19.12)![equation](images/c19-math-0012.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8796;</mo> <mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mi> <mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo> <mi>L</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>L</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

Accordingly, the one‐slot conditional Lyapunov *drift‐plus‐penalty* function is shown as follows:

(19.13)![equation](images/c19-math-0013.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi> <mi>V</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>V</mi> <mi mathvariant="double-struck">E</mi> <mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo> <mi>&#966;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c19-i0122.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>&#62;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is the policy control parameter.

 

### 19.3.1 Fog‐Enabled Multi‐Tier Operations Scheduling (FEMOS) Algorithm

 

#### Dynamic Online Bandwidth Allocation (DOBA)

To solve Problem ![images](images/c19-i0123.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">P</mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> based on the Lyapunov optimization method Neely ([2010](#c19.xhtml#c19-bib-0034)), it needs to design an algorithm to minimize the upper bound of the *Lyapunov drift‐plus‐penalty* term in each time slot. Ignoring the constant components in the upper bound of ![images](images/c19-i0124.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><mi>V</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and rearranging them, the upper‐bound minimization problem is converted to:

(19.14)![equation](images/c19-math-0014.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <munder> <mi mathvariant="normal">min</mi> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> A</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#957;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> B</mi> </mrow> </munder> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <munder> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">U</mi> </mrow> </munder> <mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""> <mrow> <mi>V</mi> <mo>+</mo> <msubsup> <mi>Q</mi> <mi>u</mi> <mtext>sum</mtext> </msubsup> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </mfenced> <msub> <mi>&#956;</mi> <mi>u</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

Note that ![images](images/c19-i0125.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>u</mi><mtext>sum</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is observed at the beginning of each time slot, which can be viewed as constant per time slot. Therefore the upper‐bound minimization only depends on ![images](images/c19-i0126.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, which involves the FAN assignment and bandwidth allocation. For convenience, we define ![images](images/c19-i0127.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8796;</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>u</mi><mtext>sum</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, which is constant per time slot. From the definition of ![images](images/c19-i0128.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> in Eq. ([19.4](#c19.xhtml#c19-disp-0004)), the upper‐bound minimization of ![images](images/c19-i0129.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><mi>V</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is transferred to the following equivalent problem:

(19.15)![equation](images/c19-math-0015.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi mathvariant="script">P</mi> <mtext>AR</mtext> </msub> <mo>:</mo> <munder> <mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> A</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#957;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> B</mi> </mrow> </munder> <munder> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">H</mi> </mrow> </munder> <munder> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">U</mi> </mrow> </munder> <msub> <mi>W</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub> <mi>&#957;</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

![images](images/c19-i0130.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="script">P</mi><mtext>AR</mtext></msub></mrow></math> is a joint optimization problem of access node assignment and bandwidth allocation. The main idea of the proposed FEMOS algorithm is to solve the deterministic optimization problem ![images](images/c19-i0131.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="script">P</mi><mtext>AR</mtext></msub></mrow></math> in each time slot. By doing so, the number of requests waiting in the queues can be maintained at a small level, and network throughput can be maximized at the same time.

Note that ![images](images/c19-i0132.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="script">P</mi><mtext>AR</mtext></msub></mrow></math> is a nonlinear integer programming problem, for which the computational complexity of the brute‐force search is prohibitive. By exploiting the structure information of ![images](images/c19-i0133.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="script">P</mi><mtext>AR</mtext></msub></mrow></math>, we transfer problem ![images](images/c19-i0134.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="script">P</mi><mtext>AR</mtext></msub></mrow></math> to the following problem ![images](images/c19-i0135.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext>AR</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math>, which is proven equivalent with ![images](images/c19-i0136.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="script">P</mi><mtext>AR</mtext></msub></mrow></math>:

(19.16)![equation](images/c19-math-0016.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mtable columnalign="right left left"> <mtr> <mtd class="eqnarray-1"> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="script">P</mi> <mtext>AR</mtext> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msubsup> <mo>:</mo> <munder> <mi mathvariant="normal">max</mi> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold">X</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </munder> </mtd> <mtd class="eqnarray-2"/> <mtd class="eqnarray-3"> <munder> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">H</mi> </mrow> </munder> <munder> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">U</mi> </mrow> </munder> <msub> <mi>W</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd class="eqnarray-1"> <mtext>s.t.</mtext> </mtd> <mtd class="eqnarray-2"/> <mtd class="eqnarray-3"> <munder> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">U</mi> </mrow> </munder> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8804;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mspace width="1em"/> <mo>&#8704;</mo> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">H</mi> <mo>,</mo> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd/> <mtd class="eqnarray-2"/> <mtd class="eqnarray-3"> <munder> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">H</mi> </mrow> </munder> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8804;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mo>&#8704;</mo> <mi>u</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script">H</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mspace width="1em"/> <mspace width="1em"/> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo> <mo>,</mo> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mrow> </math> 

and the corresponding bandwidth allocation for each UT ![images](images/c19-i0137.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="script"> U</mi></mrow></math> can be expressed as follows:

(19.17)![equation](images/c19-math-0017.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>&#957;</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced open="{" close="" separators=""> <mrow> <mtable> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="left"> <mn>1</mn> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="left"> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mrow> <mi>u</mi> <mi>h</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mo>&#8704;</mo> <mi>h</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> H</mi> <mo>,</mo> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr columnalign="left"> <mtd columnalign="left"> <mn>0</mn> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="left"> <mtext>otherwise</mtext> <mo>.</mo> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mrow> </mfenced> </mrow> </math>  

#### Centralized Assignment of Access Node (CAAN)

The dynamic assignment of FANs in each time slot can be obtained by solving the problem ![images](images/c19-i0138.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> P</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext>AR</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math>. Note that the constraint of maximum connectable UTs for each FAN in ![images](images/c19-i0139.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> P</mi></mrow><mtext>AR</mtext></msub></mrow></math> is ![images](images/c19-i0140.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></math>, while it reduces to 1 in ![images](images/c19-i0141.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> P</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext>AR</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math>.

To solve ![images](images/c19-i0142.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> P</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext>AR</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> efficiently, we demonstrate that the problem ![images](images/c19-i0143.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> P</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext>AR</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> can be formulated as the maximization of a normalized modular function subject to the intersection of two partition matroid constraints in the following. This structure can be exploited to design computationally efficient algorithms for Problem ![images](images/c19-i0144.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="script">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext>AR</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> with provable approximation gaps.

 

#### FEMOS Algorithm

The proposed FEMOS algorithm is summarized in Algorithm 1, which will be implemented at both the FCN tier and the FAN tier in practice. Specifically, in each time slot, within the global network information and queue length of each request buffer, the FCN will execute CAAN by run the greedy FAN assignment algorithm. The assignment decision is then transmitted to the FAN tier. Next, each FAN performs the DOBA independently and schedule the service rate for the associated UT under full efficient scheduling policy. Finally, the FCN updates the request buffers for each UT, the length of which will influence operations scheduling in the next slot.

![](images/c19-gra-0001.png)

Interestingly, a closer inspection of ![images](images/c19-i0145.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> P</mi></mrow><mrow><mtext>AR</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> reveals that in each time slot, each FAN can associate with at most only one UT, and the number of UTs that can dynamically associate with FANs depends on the number of FANs, which is ![images](images/c19-i0146.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo><mi mathvariant="script"> H</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#124;</mo></mrow></math>. What makes our greedy FAN assignment algorithm outstanding from the common assignment method, which directly select FAN with the best channel condition for each UT or each FAN associates with the UT with the longest queue length, is that we provide a quantitative analysis and selection method for UT‐FAN association. In each time slot, the association between UTs and FANs depends on corresponding UT‐FAN pair gain ![images](images/c19-i0147.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>u</mi><mtext>sum</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. The greedy FAN assignment algorithm greedily selects the UT‐FAN pair with the largest ![images](images/c19-i0148.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> within the feasible set. For each FAN ![images](images/c19-i0149.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></math>, it will associate with one UT with either large queue backlog or good channel condition. If ![images](images/c19-i0150.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow></math> is small, i.e. ![images](images/c19-i0151.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>&#8810;</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>u</mi><mtext>sum</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, both the queue backlog and the channel condition will determine the decision about UT‐FAN association. The FAN ![images](images/c19-i0152.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> will associate with UT with largest ![images](images/c19-i0153.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>u</mi><mtext>sum</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Conversely, if ![images](images/c19-i0154.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow></math> is large enough, i.e. ![images](images/c19-i0155.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>&#8811;</mo><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>u</mi><mtext>sum</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, the FAN ![images](images/c19-i0156.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> will more effectively invoke the willingness to associate with a UT with a good channel condition ![images](images/c19-i0157.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Under large ![images](images/c19-i0158.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow></math>, the UT with weak channel conditions cannot access the network for a long time, leading to large accumulated queue length and influence on the UT‐FAN decision in turn. Therefore, the parameter ![images](images/c19-i0159.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow></math> actually controls the FANs' willingness to serve UTs, i.e. performing UT‐FAN association. In other words, it controls the trade‐off between network throughput and transmission delay.

 

### 19.3.2 Theoretical and Numerical Analysis

 

#### 19.3.2.1 Theoretical Analysis

We provide the main theoretical results for FEMOS, which characterize the lower bounds for average network throughput as well as the upper bounds for the average sum queue length of the requests of all the UTs. Additionally, the trade‐off between the network average throughput and average delay will also be revealed.
