# 21  
Deep Multi‐Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Edge Caching

*M. Cenk Gursoy Chen Zhong and Senem Velipasalar*

*Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Syracuse University, Syracuse, New York, USA*

 

Wireless edge caching is considered one of the key techniques to reduce data traffic congestion in backhaul links. This chapter is devoted to the application of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) strategies to edge caching at both small base stations and user equipment (UE). Organized into seven sections, this chapter first presents the motivation and background on wireless edge caching. [Sections 21.2](#c21.xhtml#c21-sec-0003) and [21.3](#c21.xhtml#c21-sec-0007) address system modelling and problem formulation for different cellular deployment scenarios. In [Section 21.4](#c21.xhtml#c21-sec-0011), we present a multi‐agent actor‐critic DRL framework for edge caching with the goal to increase the cache hit rate and reduce transmission delay. By providing extensive simulation results, [Section 21.5](#c21.xhtml#c21-sec-0012) focuses on demonstrating the performance improvements with the proposed DRL policies and provides comparisons with the least recently used (LRU), least frequently used (LFU), and first‐in‐first‐out (FIFO) caching strategies when caching is performed at small base stations. In terms of working principles and caching performance, [Section 21.6](#c21.xhtml#c21-sec-0021) further compares the DRL with naive and probabilistic caching policies when caching is performed at UEs. [Section 21.7](#c21.xhtml#c21-sec-0029) includes further discussion and conclusions.

 

## 21.1 Introduction

During the past decade, explosive growth in the number of smart devices has led to unprecedented increase in the demand on rich‐media services, which generally require higher system capacity and data rates, making it even more challenging to satisfy the ever‐growing data traffic. As summarized in Cisco Visual Networking Index, from 2012–2017, overall mobile data traffic has experienced 17‐fold growth. This growth is primarily due to the increase in the mobile multimedia traffic, which is expected to grow further. For instance, it is predicted that video traffic will experience a ninefold increase by 2022 and will account for ![images](images/c21-i0001.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mn>79</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></math> of total mobile traffic. However, the increase in the mobile network connection speed, which is projected to grow threefold, will not be adequate to satisfy users' demands on high‐quality streaming services. To reduce data traffic congestion in backhaul links, content caching has been proposed and is being envisioned as one of the key components of next‐generation wireless networks (Jaber et al. ([2016](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0011))).

With these motivations and to better serve the users, content‐caching strategies have been studied recently. As noted before, content caching is considered a key technique to reduce data traffic by enabling content server nodes to store a part of popular content locally, so that when the cached content is requested, the server can deliver content directly to users or to the next content server node in the route to users and reduce the latency compared to requesting content from upper‐level servers. Based on this idea and considering different content server architectures, several caching strategies have been proposed and investigated. Considering the central content servers, such as the baseband unit in cloud radio access networks (C‐RANs), centralized coded caching and delivery schemes are presented by Yan et al. ([2017](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0036)) and Yang et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0037)). For decentralized caching, in‐network caching at the content delivery network (CDN) server is widely adopted to reduce data congestion near content servers. The placement of the in‐network cache usually involves a routing problem in CDNs. Dehghan et al. ([2017](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0006)) and Xu et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0035)) proposed joint caching and routing polices to minimize the service delay. Even though CDNs have been shown to reduce data traffic, they can hardly handle the growing mobile data traffic because it is inevitable that content has to be transmitted through CDN nodes before arriving at the user.

More recently, proactive caching at the wireless network edge, such as at small base stations and UE, is proposed. This technique makes it possible to have popular content to be placed closer to end users and be directly transmitted, which can effectively reduce the time for routing in CDNs, and apparently save a considerable amount of waiting time for users and offload a portion of the data traffic at the CDN. The architectures and challenges of caching techniques are summarized in several comprehensive survey papers (see e.g. Lei et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0019)), Wang et al. ([2017](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0032)) and Liu et al. ([2016](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0024))). Zhang et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0038)) and Li et al. ([2018b](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0023)) studied edge‐caching policies aimed at minimizing transmission delay for the base station and device‐to‐device (D2D) users. Additionally, research on hierarchical caching has recently been conducted. For instance, in studies by Kwak et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0015)), Chen et al. ([2017b](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0004)), Tran et al. ([2017](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0031)), hybrid content‐caching schemes for joint content‐caching control at the baseband unit and radio remote heads are presented. Li et al. ([2018a](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0022)) proposed an edge hierarchical caching policy for caching at the small base station and UE. Tandon and Simeone ([2016](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0030)) and Koh et al. ([2017](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0013)) considered delivery latency in fog radio access networks (F‐RANs) and presented latency‐centric caching policies. In the same context, Azimi et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0001)) proposed an online caching policy. Furthermore, the edge‐caching problem is also considered jointly with other problems. For example, Lee and Molisch ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0017)) jointly considered the caching policy and cooperation distance design in a base station–assisted wireless D2D caching network, and Chen et al. ([2017a](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0003)) addressed joint optimization of caching and scheduling policies.

In the literature, different methods have been applied to determine optimal caching policies. For the case of decentralized caching, Kvaternik et al. ([2016](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0014)) presented a decentralized optimization method for the design of caching strategies that aimed at minimizing energy consumption of the network, while Wang et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0033)) proposed a decentralized framework for proactive caching according to blockchains from a game‐theoretic point of view. In a study by Zhou et al. ([2017](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0041)), caching and multi‐cast problems are jointly solved using dynamic programming. A belief propagation algorithm for caching in D2D networks is presented by Hao et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0010)), and a clustering approach is studied by Zhang et al. ([2016](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0039)). Moreover, machine learning (ML) techniques are also applied in this field. Leconte et al. ([2016](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0016)) proposed an age‐based threshold policy that caches all content that has been requested more than a threshold. Furthermore, popularity‐based content‐caching policies named StreamCache and PopCaching were studied by Li et al. ([2016b](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0021)) and Li et al. ([2016a](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0020)), respectively. Chang et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0002)) investigated the application of ML methods to content replacement problems.

In this chapter, we focus on edge‐caching policies based on DRL methods. For edge caching at both small base stations and UEs, caching policy is driven by content popularity. Therefore, knowing the content popularity is key to solve the caching problem. In previous works, content popularity is either assumed to be known to the content server as presented by Wang et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0033)), ElBamby et al. ([2014](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0007)), or is estimated before caching actions as proposed by Zhu et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0042)), Li et al. ([2018b](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0023)). The former assumption makes the framework less practical when content popularity is time‐varying, and frequent estimation of content popularity or the arrival intensity of user requests will lead to the consumption of significant amount of resources and time. To avoid such drawbacks, ML methods are introduced to determine efficient caching policies. For example, Lei et al. ([2017](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0018)) trained a deep neural network in order to identify the optimal caching algorithm. And different DRL algorithms are used to find caching strategies that can better adapt to the changing environment. Sadeghi et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0026)) implemented a Q‐learning algorithm to find the optimal caching policy. In studies by Zhong et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0040)) and Wei et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0034)), the focus is the use of actor‐critic DRL frameworks for caching. And for cooperative caching policies in decentralized caching networks, multi‐agent Q‐learning solutions were studied by Sung et al. ([2016](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0029)) and Jiang et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0012)). Song et al. ([2017](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0028)) and Sengupta et al. ([2014](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0027)) presented two different multi‐armed bandit–based caching schemes.

As seen in previous studies, content popularity distribution is always critical in solving the content‐caching problem. In DRL algorithms, the agent needs to observe enough features of the environment to ensure the accuracy of its decisions. To better address this issue, this chapter presents a deep actor‐critic reinforcement learning (RL) multi‐agent framework for cooperative edge caching (see e.g. studies by Lowe et al. ([2017](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0025)), Foerster et al. ([2016](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0008)), Gupta et al. ([2017](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0009)) for multi‐agent DRL). However, before the details on this multi‐agent framework, we first provide the related system models and problem formulations.

 

## 21.2 System Model

We consider two different network models described in the following subsections.

 

### 21.2.1 Multi‐Cell Network Model

As shown in [Figure 21.1](#c21.xhtml#c21-fig-0001), in this subsection we introduce a communication network with a cloud data center and ![images](images/c21-i0002.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> base stations. It is assumed that the data center has sufficient storage space to cache all content files, while each base station has a fixed cache capacity of ![images](images/c21-i0003.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>. All base stations can connect with the cloud data center and request files from it. And each base station decides whether to cache a file or not. A base station is assumed to cover a fixed circular cellular region with the corresponding base station at the center. We assume that the radii of the cells are fixed and all users in the cell can access the corresponding base station. There are ![images](images/c21-i0004.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>U</mi></mrow></math> users randomly distributed in the system, and they are located in at least one cellular region covered by a base station to ensure service. We assume that in a given time slot, the users' locations do not change and those located at overlapped regions can be served by any one of the corresponding base stations. Users have their own preferences for content, and in each time slot each user can request only one content file. We denote the total number of content files as ![images](images/c21-i0005.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></math>, and use the content ID to denote requests for corresponding content. Also, in each operation cycle, users request a content based on their own preferences. The requests are sent to all base stations that can connect with the user, and the base station with the minimum transmission delay will finally transmit the content file to the user. In the meantime, all base stations will update their caches to minimize the average transmission delay based on users' requests. When making caching decisions, the base stations will compete with each other to get the chance to transmit and also cooperate with each other to reduce overall transmission delay.

![Figure 21.1 Multi‐cell network model.](images/c21f001.jpg)

[Figure 21.1](#c21.xhtml#R_c21-fig-0001) Multi‐cell network model.

 

### 21.2.2 Single‐Cell Network Model with D2D Communication

In this subsection, we introduce the single‐cell model with users having D2D communication capabilities. To offload data traffic from the base station, UE is assumed to be equipped with caches. In this setting, we consider a communication network with one base station and ![images](images/c21-i0006.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>U</mi></mrow></math> users, and each user is equipped with one cache‐enabled mobile device. To distinguish users and cache nodes, we define ![images](images/c21-i0007.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> as the number of local cache nodes, and in this case we have ![images](images/c21-i0008.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>U</mi></mrow></math>. As shown in [Figure 21.2](#c21.xhtml#c21-fig-0002), users are randomly distributed in the cellular region covered by the base station. The cellular region is described by a circle with the base station at the center, and the radius of the cell is ![images](images/c21-i0009.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow></math>. In this system, all users are able to communicate with the base station, and each user can also communicate in D2D mode with other users within a distance ![images](images/c21-i0010.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow></math>, and ![images](images/c21-i0011.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>&#60;</mo> <msub><mi>d</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow></math>. We assume that each UE has a fixed cache size ![images](images/c21-i0012.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> C</mi></mrow></math> that can be updated depending on users' requests for content. Therefore, to minimize data traffic flows to the base station, when a user requests a content, it will first check the cache at its own equipment. If the requested content is cached, the user can serve itself directly and no traffic will be generated. If, on the other hand, the content is not cached by the user itself, caches of all other users that can communicate with the user in D2D mode will be checked, and if the content can be transmitted in D2D mode, the data traffic will be generated from the corresponding user. If none of the D2D transmitters has this content cached, the user will request the content from the base station. We assume that in a given time slot, users' locations do not change and those that can communicate in D2D mode with multiple users can be served by any one of the corresponding D2D transmitters. Users have their own preferences for content, and in each time slot a user can request only one content file. Let us again denote the total number of content files as ![images](images/c21-i0013.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></math>, and use the content ID to denote requests for corresponding content. In each operation cycle, users request a content based on their own preferences. The requests are sent to all D2D transmitters that can connect with the user, and all users update their caches. When making the caching decision, users need to consider their own preferences as well as potential collaborative file exchanges with other users in D2D mode in order to maximize the cache hit rates.

![Figure 21.2 Single‐cell network model with device‐to‐device communication.](images/c21f002.jpg)

[Figure 21.2](#c21.xhtml#R_c21-fig-0002) Single‐cell network model with device‐to‐device communication.

 

### 21.2.3 Action Space

Henceforth, in order to unify the descriptions and analysis of both cellular network models described, in the multi‐cell network model we consider base stations as the local content servers and the cloud data center as an upper‐level server. Correspondingly, in the single‐cell network model with D2D communications, we consider cache‐enabled UEs as local content servers and the single base station in the model as the upper‐level server.

To find an edge‐caching policy for these two network models, let us consider an actor‐critic RL–based multi‐agent framework. In this framework, there are ![images](images/c21-i0014.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> actor networks and one centralized critic network. We consider each local cache server an agent that adopts one of the actor networks to seek its own caching policy. And we assume there are control channels that allow local content servers to send the caching state and data traffic parameters to the upper‐level server, so that the upper‐level server can act as the centralized critic to evaluate the overall caching state. Similarly as in the study by Zhong et al. ([2018](#c21.xhtml#c21-bib-0040)), in each operation cycle, the agent can either keep the cache state the same or replace unpopular content files with the popular ones. However, since there can be more than one request arriving at a local content server at the same time, the agent needs to jointly decide which cached content will be deleted and which content requested by which user will be cached. We define the action space as ![images](images/c21-i0015.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> A</mi></mrow></math>, and let ![images](images/c21-i0016.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="{" close="}" separators=""><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> D</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></mrow></math>, where ![images](images/c21-i0017.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>&#957;</mi></msub></mrow></math> denotes a valid action. In our case, ![images](images/c21-i0018.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math> indicates that the current cache state is unchanged. For ![images](images/c21-i0019.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#957;</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="script"> D</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo></mrow></math>, we define ![images](images/c21-i0020.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> D</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""><mfrac linethickness="0"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> C</mi></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mn>1</mn></mfrac></mfenced><mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""><mfrac linethickness="0"><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mn>1</mn></mfrac></mfenced></mrow></math>, where ![images](images/c21-i0021.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> C</mi></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> is the number of files in the cache of local content server ![images](images/c21-i0022.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>, and ![images](images/c21-i0023.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> is the number of users that can connect with the local content server ![images](images/c21-i0024.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>. So each ![images](images/c21-i0025.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>&#957;</mi></msub></mrow></math> stands for a possible combination to replace one of ![images](images/c21-i0026.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> C</mi></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> cached content files with one of ![images](images/c21-i0027.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> currently requested content files. In each time slot, all agents must select their own action from the action space ![images](images/c21-i0028.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> A</mi></mrow></math> and execute.

 

## 21.3 Problem Formulation

 

### 21.3.1 Cache Hit Rate

In this part, we evaluate the caching policy in terms of overall cache hit rate, which is defined as

![equation](images/c21-math-0001.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>U</mi></munderover><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mi>U</mi></mfrac></mrow></math> 

where ![images](images/c21-i0029.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>U</mi></mrow></math> is the total number of users, and ![images](images/c21-i0030.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> is given by

![equation](images/c21-math-0002.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="{" close="" separators=""><mrow><mtable columnalign="left"><mtr><mtd class="array"><mn>1</mn><mspace width="11.38092pt"/><mtext>if user</mtext><mspace width="0.3em"/><mi>i</mi><mspace width="0.2em"/><mtext>is served by the local content server</mtext></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="array"><mn>0</mn><mspace width="11.38092pt"/><mtext>if user</mtext><mspace width="0.3em"/><mi>i</mi><mspace width="0.2em"/><mtext>is served by the upper&#8208;level server</mtext></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> 

Basically, the cache hit rate shows the percentage of requests served by the local content servers. The cache hit rate maximization problem can be formulated as follows:

![equation](images/c21-math-0003.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mtable columnalign="left"><mtr><mtd columnalign="right"><mtext mathvariant="bold">P1:</mtext><mspace width="28.45274pt"/></mtd><mtd columnalign="left"><munder><mtext>Maximize</mtext><mrow><mi>&#38;b.Upsi;</mi></mrow></munder><mspace width="34.14322pt"/><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="right"/><mtd columnalign="left"><mtext>Subject to</mtext><mspace width="19.91684pt"/><munderover><mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>M</mi></munderover><msub><mi>&#965;</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8804;</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> C</mi></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></math> 

where ![images](images/c21-i0031.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#38;b.Upsi;</mi></mrow></math> is an ![images](images/c21-i0032.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> matrix that records the caching states of the ![images](images/c21-i0033.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> local content servers, and each element ![images](images/c21-i0034.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#965;</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> in the caching state matrix is an indicator to show if the file is cached:

(21.1)![equation](images/c21-math-0004.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>&#965;</mi> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>f</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced open="{" close="" separators=""> <mrow> <mtable columnalign="left"> <mtr> <mtd class="array"> <mn>1</mn> <mspace width="11.38092pt"/> <mtext>if file</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>f</mi> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mtext>is cached at the local content server</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>i</mi> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd class="array"> <mn>0</mn> <mspace width="11.38092pt"/> <mtext>if file</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>f</mi> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mtext>is not cached at the local content server</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>i</mi> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mrow> </mfenced> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math>  

### 21.3.2 Transmission Delay

We also address the performance of the caching policy in terms of transmission delay. The transmission delay is defined as the number of time frames needed to transmit a content file, and can be expressed as

(21.2)![equation](images/c21-math-0005.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>T</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi mathvariant="normal">min</mi> <mfenced open="{" close="}" separators=""> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> <mo>:</mo> <mi>F</mi> <mo>&#8804;</mo> <munderover> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>&#954;</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> </mrow> </munderover> <msub> <mi>T</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> <mi>C</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>&#954;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> </mrow> </mfenced> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c21-i0035.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>F</mi></mrow></math> is the size of the content file to be transmitted. ![images](images/c21-i0036.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math> stands for the duration of each time frame, and ![images](images/c21-i0037.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>&#954;</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> is the instantaneous channel capacity in the ![images](images/c21-i0038.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>&#954;</mi><mtext>th</mtext></msup></mrow></math> time frame. And the channel capacity ![images](images/c21-i0039.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>&#954;</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> is expressed as

(21.3)![equation](images/c21-math-0006.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>C</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi>&#954;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mi>B</mi> <mspace width="0.2em"/> <msub> <mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> <mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""> <mrow> <mn>1</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mfrac> <mrow> <msub> <mi>P</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>B</mi> <msup> <mi>&#963;</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msup> </mrow> </mfrac> <msub> <mi>z</mi> <mi>&#954;</mi> </msub> </mrow> </mfenced> <mspace width="11.38092pt"/> <mtext>bits</mtext> <mo stretchy="false">/</mo> <mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c21-i0040.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> is the transmission power, ![images](images/c21-i0041.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> is the channel bandwidth, ![images](images/c21-i0042.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> is the noise variance, and ![images](images/c21-i0043.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>&#954;</mi></msub></mrow></math> is the magnitude square of the corresponding fading coefficient in the ![images](images/c21-i0044.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>&#954;</mi><mtext>th</mtext></msup></mrow></math> time frame. In the system, there are two types of transmitters, e.g. the cloud data center and the base stations in the multi‐cell model (and the base station and D2D‐capable users in the single‐cell model). We assume that all transmitters transmit at their maximum power level to maximize the transmission rate. The transmission power is defined as

(21.4)![equation](images/c21-math-0007.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>P</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced open="{" close="" separators=""> <mrow> <mtable columnalign="left"> <mtr> <mtd class="array"> <msub> <mi>P</mi> <mi>b</mi> </msub> <mspace width="28.45274pt"/> <mtext>if the transmitter is the upper&#8208;level server</mtext> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd class="array"> <msub> <mi>P</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> <mspace width="28.45274pt"/> <mtext>if the transmitter is the</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <msup> <mi>i</mi> <mtext>th</mtext> </msup> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mtext>local content server</mtext> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mrow> </mfenced> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

To be more concrete in the discussions and following descriptions, we specifically address the multi‐cell network model. Note that the descriptions can easily be adapted to the single cell with D2D‐capable users as well.

In the considered multi‐cell model, if user ![images](images/c21-i0045.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math> requests a content that is not cached at any base station that can connect with the user, the content file will be first transmitted from the cloud data center to base station ![images](images/c21-i0046.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>i</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover></mrow></math>, which is the closest base station to user ![images](images/c21-i0047.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math>, and then from base station ![images](images/c21-i0048.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>i</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover></mrow></math> to user ![images](images/c21-i0049.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math>. Thus, the minimum transmission delay ![images](images/c21-i0050.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math> in the case of missing file in the cache can be expressed as

(21.5)![equation](images/c21-math-0008.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>D</mi> <mo>&#94;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>j</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>T</mi> <mrow> <mi>c</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mover accent="true"> <mi>i</mi> <mo>&#94;</mo> </mover> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>T</mi> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>i</mi> <mo>&#94;</mo> </mover> <mo>,</mo> <mi>j</mi> </mrow> </msub> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c21-i0051.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>i</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover></mrow></msub></mrow></math> stands for the transmission delay from the cloud data center to base station ![images](images/c21-i0052.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>i</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover></mrow></math>, and ![images](images/c21-i0053.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>i</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is the transmission delay from base station ![images](images/c21-i0054.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>i</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover></mrow></math> to user ![images](images/c21-i0055.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math>.

However, if the requested file is cached at base station ![images](images/c21-i0056.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>, which can connect to user ![images](images/c21-i0057.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math>, the transmission delay ![images](images/c21-i0058.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math> for the case of hitting the cache can be expressed as

(21.6)![equation](images/c21-math-0009.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>D</mi> <mi>j</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>T</mi> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>j</mi> </mrow> </msub> </mrow> </math> 

Now, the transmission delay for both cases of missing and hitting the cache is known, and we define the transmission delay reduction ![images](images/c21-i0059.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math> as

(21.7)![equation](images/c21-math-0010.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi> <msub> <mi>D</mi> <mi>j</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>D</mi> <mo>&#94;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>j</mi> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>D</mi> <mi>j</mi> </msub> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

So, the average transmission delay reduction in an operation cycle is

(21.8)![equation](images/c21-math-0011.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi> <mi>D</mi> <malignmark/> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mi>U</mi> </mfrac> <munderover> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>j</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>U</mi> </munderover> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi> <msub> <mi>D</mi> <mi>j</mi> </msub> </mrow> </math> (21.9)![equation](images/c21-math-0012.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <malignmark/> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mi>U</mi> </mfrac> <munderover> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>j</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>U</mi> </munderover> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>D</mi> <mo>&#94;</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mi>j</mi> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>D</mi> <mi>j</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </math> (21.10)![equation](images/c21-math-0013.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <malignmark/> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mi>U</mi> </mfrac> <munderover> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>j</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>U</mi> </munderover> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mi>T</mi> <mrow> <mi>c</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mover accent="true"> <mi>i</mi> <mo>&#94;</mo> </mover> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>T</mi> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>i</mi> <mo>&#94;</mo> </mover> <mo>,</mo> <mi>j</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>T</mi> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>j</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c21-i0060.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>U</mi></mrow></math> is the total number of users. Now, our goal is to maximize the average transmission delay reduction, and the caching problem is formulated as follows:

(21.11)![equation](images/c21-math-0014.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mtext mathvariant="bold">P2:</mtext> <mspace width="28.45274pt"/> <munder> <mtext>Maximize</mtext> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold">&#934;</mi> </mrow> </munder> <mspace width="34.14322pt"/> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi> <mi>D</mi> </mrow> </math> (21.12)![equation](images/c21-math-0015.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mspace width="4.3em"/> <mtext>Subject to</mtext> <mspace width="19.91684pt"/> <msub> <mi>&#958;</mi> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>j</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </math> [(21.13)](#c21.xhtml#c21-R_disp-0016)![equation](images/c21-math-0016.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mspace width="4em"/> <mspace width="59.75095pt"/> <munderover> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>f</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>M</mi> </munderover> <msub> <mi>&#966;</mi> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>f</mi> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi>F</mi> <mi>f</mi> </msub> <mo>&#8804;</mo> <mi>C</mi> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c21-i0061.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">&#934;</mi></mrow></math> is an ![images](images/c21-i0062.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> matrix that records the caching states of the ![images](images/c21-i0063.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> local content servers, and each element ![images](images/c21-i0064.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#966;</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> in the caching state matrix is an indicator to show if the file is cached:

(21.14)![equation](images/c21-math-0017.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>&#966;</mi> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>f</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced open="{" close="" separators=""> <mrow> <mtable columnalign="left"> <mtr> <mtd class="array"> <mn>1</mn> <mspace width="11.38092pt"/> <mtext>if the file</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>f</mi> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mtext>is cached at the local content server</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>i</mi> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd class="array"> <mn>0</mn> <mspace width="11.38092pt"/> <mtext>if the file</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>f</mi> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mtext>is not cached at the local content server</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>i</mi> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mrow> </mfenced> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

![images](images/c21-i0065.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow></math> is the size of file ![images](images/c21-i0066.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow></math>. If, without loss of generality, we assume all files have the same size, the condition in Eq. ([21.13](#c21.xhtml#c21-disp-0016)) can be rewritten as

(21.15)![equation](images/c21-math-0018.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <munderover> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false" movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>f</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>M</mi> </munderover> <msub> <mi>&#966;</mi> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>f</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8804;</mo> <mi mathvariant="script"> C</mi> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c21-i0067.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> C</mi></mrow></math> is the maximum number of files that can be stored at each base station and ![images](images/c21-i0068.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#958;</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is an indicator describing if user ![images](images/c21-i0069.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math> is in the area covered by base station ![images](images/c21-i0070.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>:

(21.16)![equation](images/c21-math-0019.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>&#958;</mi> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>j</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced open="{" close="" separators=""> <mrow> <mtable columnalign="left"> <mtr> <mtd class="array"> <mn>1</mn> <mspace width="5.69046pt"/> <mtext>if user</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>j</mi> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mtext>can connect to local content server</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>i</mi> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd class="array"> <mn>0</mn> <mspace width="5.69046pt"/> <mtext>if user</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>j</mi> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mtext>cannot connect to local content server</mtext> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi>i</mi> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mrow> </mfenced> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math>  

## 21.4 Deep Actor‐Critic Framework for Content Caching

Having presented the previous system models and problem formulations, let us introduce a multi‐agent actor‐critic framework based on the partially observable Markov decision processes with ![images](images/c21-i0071.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> agents, where the critic network ![images](images/c21-i0072.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="monospace">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c21-i0073.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> actors ![images](images/c21-i0074.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>&#960;</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c21-i0075.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></math>, are parameterized by ![images](images/c21-i0076.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#952;</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo></mrow></math>.

*Actor*: The actor is defined as a function to seek a caching policy ![images](images/c21-i0077.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#960;</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo></mrow></math>, which can map the observation of the agent to a valid action chosen from the action space ![images](images/c21-i0078.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> A</mi></mrow></math>. In each time slot, agent ![images](images/c21-i0079.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math> will select an action ![images](images/c21-i0080.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> based on its own observation ![images](images/c21-i0081.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> and policy ![images](images/c21-i0082.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math>:

![equation](images/c21-math-0020.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> 

*Critic*: The critic is employed to estimate the value function ![images](images/c21-i0083.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="monospace">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, where ![images](images/c21-i0084.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="monospace">x</mi></mrow></math> stands for the observation of all agents, i.e. ![images](images/c21-i0085.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="monospace">x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo></mrow></math>. At time instant ![images](images/c21-i0086.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>, after actions ![images](images/c21-i0087.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo></mrow></math> are chosen by the actor networks, the agents will execute the actions in the environment and send the current observation ![images](images/c21-i0088.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="monospace">x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> along with feedback from the environment to the critic. The feedback includes reward ![images](images/c21-i0089.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> and the next time instant observation ![images](images/c21-i0090.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="monospace">x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. Then, the critic can calculate the temporal difference (TD) error:

![equation](images/c21-math-0021.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>&#948;</mi><mrow><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mi>&#952;</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>&#947;</mi><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="monospace">x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>V</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="monospace">x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> 

where ![images](images/c21-i0091.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#947;</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is the discount factor.

*Update*: The critic is updated by minimizing the least squares temporal difference (LSTD):

![equation](images/c21-math-0022.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>V</mi><mo>&#42;</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">arg</mi><munder><mi mathvariant="normal">min</mi><mi>V</mi></munder><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>&#948;</mi><mrow><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mi>&#952;</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> 

where ![images](images/c21-i0092.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>V</mi><mo>&#42;</mo></msup></mrow></math> denotes the optimal value function.

Actor ![images](images/c21-i0093.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math> is updated by policy gradient. Here we use TD error to compute the policy gradient:

![equation](images/c21-math-0023.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mi>J</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>&#960;</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mrow><mo>&#8711;</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><msub><mrow><mi>&#960;</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>&#948;</mi><mrow><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mi>&#952;</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> 

where ![images](images/c21-i0094.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>&#960;</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> denotes the score of action ![images](images/c21-i0095.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> under the current policy. Then, the actor network *i* can be updated using the gradient decent method:

![equation](images/c21-math-0024.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#8592;</mo><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>&#945;</mi><msub><mrow><mo>&#8711;</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><msub><mrow><mi>&#960;</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>&#952;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>&#948;</mi><mrow><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mi>&#952;</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> 

The detailed steps of these processes are shown in Algorithm 1, and the structure is shown in [Figure 21.3](#c21.xhtml#c21-fig-0003).

![Figure 21.3 Deep actor‐critic‐based multi‐agent structure.](images/c21f003.jpg)

[Figure 21.3](#c21.xhtml#R_c21-fig-0003) Deep actor‐critic‐based multi‐agent structure.

![](images/c21-gra-0001.png)

*Environment*: To perform the experiments, we consider wireless cellular networks with one upper‐level server, ![images](images/c21-i0096.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow></math> local content servers, and ![images](images/c21-i0097.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>U</mi></mrow></math> users distributed in the servers' coverage regions. Allowing the agents to make their own caching decisions and cooperate with each other, the framework becomes a centralized critic network together with a decentralized actor network. Therefore, the agents will feed the actor network with their own observations and feed the critic network with the complete state space.

*Agents' Observation and State Space*: As noted before, the multi‐agent actor‐critic framework is based on a partially observable Markov decision process. Each agent ![images](images/c21-i0098.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c21-i0099.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></math>, can only observe the requests arriving at itself, and can select its own action only based on the observation ![images](images/c21-i0100.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math>. In the environment, agent ![images](images/c21-i0101.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math> can observe the content's features through its local request history. And for the centralized critic, the state space is defined as ![images](images/c21-i0102.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="monospace">x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo></mrow></math>.

*Feature Space*: The feature space consists of three components: short‐term feature ![images](images/c21-i0103.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> F</mi></mrow><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></math>, medium‐term feature ![images](images/c21-i0104.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> F</mi></mrow><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow></math>, and long‐term feature ![images](images/c21-i0105.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="script"> F</mi></mrow><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></math>, which represent the total number of requests for each content in a specific short‐term, medium‐term, or long‐term, respectively. These features are updated as new requests arrive at agents. Then, we let ![images](images/c21-i0106.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, for ![images](images/c21-i0107.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mfenced open="{" close="}" separators=""><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c21-i0108.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo></mrow></math> denote the feature of a specific content within a specific term, where ![images](images/c21-i0109.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></math> is the total number of content files. Thus, the observation for each agent ![images](images/c21-i0110.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math> is defined as
